subject: Performance SLOs & Benchmark Methodology - follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@edgefin.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Performance SLOs & Benchmark Methodology - follow-up

Thanks again for taking the time today, Sam - really appreciate the deep dive on EdgeFin's latency and streaming requirements. Quick recap from our end and suggested next steps so we can scope a reproducible benchmark: 

Summary of requirements (from call):
- 95th percentile tail latency target: <= 350ms for single-turn text generation (max prompt + gen length ~ 256 tokens)
- Throughput/Concurrency: baseline 200 QPS sustained, with planned peak bursts to 600 QPS during end-of-day batch jobs
- Streaming: real-time token-level streaming to client with average per-token interval target <= 20ms
- Concurrency characteristics: up to 500 concurrent open connections with streaming enabled; KV cache warm-up expected across hot prefixes
- Accuracy/Quality constraints: no more than 3% drop in task-specific eval F1 relative to your baseline model (EdgeFin-v1)

Proposed next steps:
1) We prepare a formal benchmark methodology doc (prompt sets + eval harness + measurement definitions) and share it for review - target by Wed 24 Feb.
2) You share any proprietary prompt sets or evaluation labels you want included, or we can use an agreed public-style dataset as a proxy.
3) We run a pilot benchmark in our pre-prod cluster (dedicated instance) and share raw logs/measurements for reproducibility.

Would you be able to confirm: (a) the exact payload size distribution you expect for the streaming use case, and (b) whether we should prioritize p95 latency under cold cache vs. warmed-KV-cache scenarios?

I'm attaching a short proposal outline and a first-pass prompt set. If that looks good, we'll schedule a 30-minute handoff with our infra engineer (Dylan) to coordinate credentials and test traffic patterns.

[Attachment: edgefin-benchmark-proposal.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)]
[Attachment: edgefin-prompt-set-v1.csv (CSV, 45KB)]

Best,

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@edgefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@edgefin.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs & Benchmark Methodology - follow-up

Thanks Marissa - good recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Payload distribution: about 60% of requests are short prompts (< 64 tokens), 30% mid-length (64-256), and 10% long (256-1024). For streaming, most traffic is short/mid requests with token-by-token streaming to the web client.

2) Cold vs warmed cache: p95 under warm-KV-cache is our primary business SLO for interactive flows. Cold-cache behavior matters for batch/scale-up events but can be a secondary metric.

3) Concurrency nuance: When we say 500 concurrent open connections, that maps to ~350 active streaming sessions (token streaming), plus ~150 idle/keep-alive connections. We use HTTP/2 for streaming.

4) Reproducibility: we need the benchmark to include raw measurement logs and a seeded randomization for prompt order so we can reproduce runs in our environment. Can you confirm the eval harness will be open and versioned?

If you can share the methodology doc and the eval harness link, we'll review and flag anything sensitive before sharing labeled data. Also happy to set up a quick sync with your infra team.

Thanks - Sam
Sam Patel

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2027 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs & Benchmark Methodology - follow-up

Appreciate the details, Sam - that's exactly the kind of breakdown we needed. A few concrete commitments from our side: 

- Methodology doc: attached is the proposed methodology with definitions for latency (p50/p90/p95/p99), throughput (sustained vs. burst), concurrency accounting, streaming inter-token timing, and reproducibility steps. We've included a seeded-run option in the harness so orders and RNG are consistent.

- Eval harness: public repo (read-only) with a reproducible Docker image and a CI workflow - see the link below. We'll tag the release we use for your benchmark and include instructions to replay results locally.

- Prompt sets: included as a CSV (edgefin-prompt-set-v1.csv) for an initial pass. If you provide labeled references, we'll plug them into the same harness.

Next operational steps: 
1) Review the attached methodology and prompt set.
2) If OK, sign off on the scope so we can schedule the pilot run in our dedicated pre-prod cluster (we estimate 2-4 hours of runtime for a full sweep at your target QPS).
3) We will provide a signed S3 bucket with logs and a manifest (SHA256) for reproducibility.

Links & artifacts:
- Drive folder (methodology + artifacts): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bEdgeFinBenchmark
- Eval harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/tree/edgefin-proposal

[Attachment: edgefin-benchmark-proposal.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)]
[Attachment: edgefin-prompt-set-v1.csv (CSV, 45KB)]

Let us know when you'd be comfortable sharing labeled eval data and any IP constraints; we can accept data under an NDA-backed S3 upload if needed. Dylan - can you coordinate the dev-access flow and provide a short checklist for EdgeFin?

Best,
Marissa
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@edgefin.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs & Benchmark Methodology - follow-up

Hi Sam - I can take point on the pilot run. Quick checklist to move to pilot:
- Access: please provide a short-lived S3 upload token or a secure share link for any labeled eval data (we prefer encrypted S3 with KMS).
- Traffic profile: share a simple CSV with per-minute QPS distribution for one typical peak day (we can also use the payload distribution Sam gave).
- Test credentials: a service API key (read-only) for the EdgeFin staging endpoint if you want us to run against your staging model; otherwise we'll run against a pinned open-model variant in our pre-prod cluster.
- Bi-weekly sync: propose a 30-min kickoff Tues 2 Mar 2027 10:00 AM PT - happy to adjust.

We'll tag the harness with a release and provide the Docker image digest and the exact script used to run the benchmark. That will include a seed for shuffling and a manifest of all prompt files.

If you'd like, we can also include a small streaming micro-benchmark early in the run (100 concurrent streaming sessions for 10 minutes) to validate inter-token latency targets before scaling to the full sweep.

Thanks - looking forward to it.

Dylan Brooks
Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
